title: 불멍 하면서 아무 말 안 해도 돼요

story.text: 경기도 외곽의 한 캠핑장에 도착하자, 규현은 캠핑 장비를 척척 꺼내며 텐트부터 쳤다. "이래 봬도 캠핑 짬밥 있는 남자예요."
story.reading: gyeong-gi-do oe-gwag-ui han kaem-ping-jang-e do-chak-ha-ja, gyu-hyeon-eun kaem-ping jang-bi-reul cheok-cheok kkeon-nae-myeo ten-teu-bu-teo chyeot-da. "i-rae bwae-do kaem-ping jjam-bap it-neun nam-ja-ye-yo."
story.en: The moment we arrived at a campground on the outskirts of Gyeonggi-do, Kyuhyun pulled out the camping gear without missing a beat and pitched the tent first. "I may not look it, but I've got serious camping experience."

story.text: 해가 완전히 저물 무렵, 그는 장작을 차곡차곡 쌓아 모닥불을 피웠다. 탁탁 튀는 불꽃 소리가 조용한 숲속에 울려 퍼졌다.
story.reading: hae-ga wan-jeon-hi jeo-mul mu-lyeop, geu-neun jang-jag-eul cha-gok-cha-gok ssah-a mo-dak-bul-eul pi-wot-da. tak-tak twi-neun bul-kkot so-ri-ga jo-yong-han sup-sog-e ul-lyeo pyeo-jyeot-da.
story.en: As the sun set completely, he stacked the firewood neatly and lit a campfire. The crackling pop of the flames echoed through the quiet forest.

story.text: 우리는 접이식 의자에 나란히 앉아 아무 말 없이 타오르는 불꽃만 바라보았다. "이게 그 유명한 불멍이라는 거예요?" 내가 묻자 규현이 작게 웃었다. "네, 아무 생각 안 해도 되는 시간이에요."
story.reading: u-ri-neun jeob-i-sik ui-ja-e na-ran-hi anj-a a-mu mal eop-si ta-o-reu-neun bul-kkot-man ba-ra-bo-at-da. "i-ge geu yu-myeong-han bul-meong-i-ra-neun geo-ye-yo?" nae-ga mut-ja gyu-hyeon-i jak-ge us-eot-da. "ne, a-mu saeng-gak an hae-do doe-neun si-gan-i-e-yo."
story.en: We sat side by side in folding chairs, silently watching the flickering flames. "Is this that famous 'fire-staring' thing everyone talks about?" I asked, and Kyuhyun gave a small laugh. "Yeah, it's time when you don't have to think about anything at all."

story.text: 한참을 그렇게 있다가 그가 나직이 입을 열었다. "이런 시간, 나쁘지 않죠? 말 안 해도 편한 사이라는 거." 평소의 능글맞음은 온데간데없이 진지한 목소리였다.
story.reading: han-cham-eul geu-reoh-ge it-da-ga geu-ga na-jig-i ib-eul yeol-eot-da. "i-reon si-gan, na-ppeu-ji an-cho? mal an hae-do pyeon-han sa-i-ra-neun geo." pyeong-so-ui neung-geul-maj-eum-eun on-de-gan-de-eob-si jin-ji-han mok-so-ri-eot-da.
story.en: After a long while like that, he spoke quietly. "Moments like this aren't so bad, right? Being the kind of friends who are comfortable even in silence." His usual smoothness had vanished; his voice was completely sincere.

story.text: 고개를 들자 나뭇가지 사이로 별자리가 선명하게 펼쳐져 있었다. "저기 저거, 국자 모양 보여요?" 그가 손끝으로 하늘을 가리켰다.
story.reading: go-gae-reul deul-ja na-mut-ga-ji sa-i-ro byeol-ja-ri-ga seon-myeong-ha-ge pyeol-chyeo-jyeo iss-eot-da. "jeo-gi jeo-geo, guk-ja mo-yang bo-yeo-yo?" geu-ga son-kkeut-eu-ro ha-neul-eul ga-ri-kyeot-da.
story.en: I looked up to find a constellation spread clearly across the sky between the branches. "See that, over there? Looks like a ladle, right?" He pointed up at the sky with his fingertip.

story.text: "여기 오길 잘했다." 내가 중얼거리듯 말하자 그가 헛기침을 하며 장작 하나를 더 불에 던져 넣었다. "그렇죠? 아가씨도 이제 좀 아네."
story.reading: "yeo-gi o-gil jal-haet-da." nae-ga jung-eol-geo-ri-deut mal-ha-ja geu-ga heot-gi-chim-eul ha-myeo jang-jag ha-na-reul deo bul-e deon-jyeo neoh-eot-da. "geu-reoh-jyo? a-ga-ssi-do i-je jom a-ne."
story.en: "Glad we came here." I murmured half to myself, and he cleared his throat and tossed another log onto the fire. "Right? Looks like you're starting to get it, miss."

story.text: 밤이 깊어질수록 텐트 옆 모닥불의 온기가 우리 사이를 더 가깝게 만들어 주는 것 같았다. 굳이 말을 하지 않아도 편안한 침묵이었다.
story.reading: bam-i gip-eo-jil-su-rok ten-teu yeop mo-dak-bul-ui on-gi-ga u-ri sa-i-reul deo ga-kkap-ge man-deul-eo ju-neun geot gat-at-da. gud-i mal-eul ha-ji an-a-do pyeon-an-han chim-muk-i-eot-da.
story.en: The deeper the night grew, the warmth from the campfire beside the tent seemed to draw us closer together. It was a comfortable silence, one that needed no words.

story.text: 불씨가 잦아들 때까지, 우리는 그렇게 나란히 앉아 있었다. 오랜 친구와 함께 보내는 이런 밤이, 나는 오래도록 그리울 것 같았다.
story.reading: bul-ssi-ga jaj-a-deul ttae-kka-ji, u-ri-neun geu-reoh-ge na-ran-hi anj-a iss-eot-da. o-raen chin-gu-wa ham-kke bo-nae-neun i-reon bam-i, na-neun o-rae-do-rok geu-ri-ul geot gat-at-da.
story.en: We sat there side by side like that until the embers finally died down. I had a feeling I'd miss nights like this — spent with an old friend — for a long time to come.

words.example_en: Shall we go camping this weekend?
Let's sit in front of the campfire and talk.

words.meaning: zoning out while staring at a fire
words.example_en: I love zoning out staring at a fire.
I'll help you pitch the tent.
What's the name of that constellation?

sentences.en: Let's just zone out by the fire tonight.
We should pitch the tent first.
